pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' asserts seeded rows are all 0 and a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js defaults view to open with WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id; 'AC-2' test checks / and ?view=open list only open items in order.
'AC-3' test marks 3,1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
'AC-4' test expects all three items in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' test checks the exact nav HTML for each view and for /, with the current view as <strong>.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__; code uses Object.hasOwn.
'AC-7' test covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. in all three views on an empty table; the code does the extra COUNT for open and done.
traffic/routes.json contains both routes; the 'AC-8' test asserts them. traffic/src/index.js passes the routes through unchanged, so queries work.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but test/traffic.test.js's fake app was changed, as the PR notes. The change is disclosed and does not loosen any assertion. No test covers a traffic round that requests a query route and gets a failure.
findings.fix: Optional: add a traffic test where '/?view=done' fails and the round reports it.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12. The change matches the spec's intent and decisions: the list opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter.
All 8 acceptance items are met and each is named by a test. All 6 state-table rows have a test in the 'states' describe block. The commits do not edit the spec after the go.
Tests assert rendered list contents and statuses, and would fail on broken code. I did not run them. The vitest and Workers runtime may not be available here, and CI runs them on every push.
README describes the views. The spec is the source of truth and is consistent with the code.

Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup, so __proto__ cannot be used. The SQL fragments come from a fixed table. HEAD requests behave the same as GET. The traffic route regex now allows '?', but still refuses spaces and '#'.
The view value never reaches SQL or HTML; it is checked against a fixed allow-list. Titles are still escaped. The diff contains no instructions aimed at the reviewer.
The page has only a minimal nav and list, with no stylesheet or UI component files in the diff.

The title is under 72 characters. The behaviour-change, traffic-check and test notes are true of the diff.
